items.title: SFI unit of UoH demands professor’s sacking over alleged casteist remarks
points: The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) unit of University of Hyderabad has demanded immediate termination of the employment of Vijaya Ramadas, associate professor in the Department of History, over alleged casteist, classist and racist remarks directed at…

In a statement, the SFI unit cited email correspondence dated April 16, 2026, in which Mr. Ramadas allegedly made derogatory remarks about the student’s caste, class and regional background, particularly referring to people from Bihar and Jharkhand as…
Portions of the purported correspondence also showed: “untouchable Dalit background; civilisationally, politcally, and economically backward state like Jharkhand; Dalit untouchable idiot”.
The emails reportedly followed a disagreement over revisions to a book chapter intended for an edited volume to be published by Bloomsbury.
The SFI unit also alleged that the professor threatened to discourage academics across India from supporting the student.
The organisation said it had submitted formal complaints to university authorities, including the Vice-Chancellor.
The affected student had also approached the university administration and the Reservation and Coordination Cell.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh weighs making father’s name optional in official documents
points: Officials of various government departments, child rights organisations, the AP Mahila Commission and NGOs on Tuesday discussed the proposal to make a father’s name optional in all official documents.

The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (APSCPCR), in association with NGOs Children India Foundation (CIF) and HELP, organised a State-level consultation on ‘Making Father’s Name Not Mandatory in Documents’ here.

Raju said the Commission welcomed the views of experts from various sectors on making a father’s name optional, particularly for children of sex workers, divorced couples and orphans, as well as those who did not wish to mention their fathers’ names in…
Mahila Commission Chairperson Rayapati Sailaja said children should not be forced to discontinue their education or be denied employment opportunities because of certain rules.

Representatives of the Education, Women Development and Child Welfare, Medical and Health, Judiciary and other departments said the government should examine the possible legal implications of the proposal and frame rules in the best interests of children.

items.title: Kerala PSC chairperson M.R. Baiju refuses to appear before Crime Branch again
points: Published - November 10, 2026 06:39 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The entrance to the Kerala Public Service Commission in Thiruvananthapuram | Photo Credit: SPECAIL ARRANGEMENT Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) chairperson M.R.

Baiju declined to appear before the Crime Branch Special Investigation Team (SIT) for questioning in connection with alleged irregularities in examinations to senior posts in the State Planning Board again on Tuesday (November 10).
He has reiterated his stance that he will appear for questioning only after the Kerala High Court delivers its order on the petition challenging the Crime Branch investigation.
The PSC chairperson was directed to appear at the Crime Branch headquarters in the State capital at 2.30 p.m.
However, he communicated to the SIT that he would wait for the High Court’s decision before cooperating with the questioning.
The investigation team is expected to bring the matter to the attention of the High Court.
This is the third notice issued by the Crime Branch to Mr. Baiju in connection with the case.

items.title: Naidu cautions Ministers against complacency after local poll victory
points: Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan shake hands before attending a Cabinet meeting at the State Secretariat in Velagapudi, Amaravati on Tuesday.
Setting the 2029 Assembly elections as the next major political target, Chief Minister N.

Chandrababu Naidu has cautioned Ministers against becoming complacent following the NDA’s emphatic victory in the local body elections and urged them to focus on governance and fulfilling the government’s promises.

At a Cabinet meeting chaired by him in Amaravati on Tuesday, Mr. Naidu advised Ministers to remain restrained and vigilant, stressing that the electoral success should increase their responsibility towards the people.
He also called for steps to bring down the prices of essential commodities, particularly rice, while noting that vegetable prices had declined.
Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar said rice was being sold at subsidised prices through Rythu Bazaars to provide relief to consumers.

items.title: DVAC launches probe into book purchase ‘irregularities’ at Tamil Nadu’s Periyar Arivulagam, Anna Centenary Library
points: Updated - November 10, 2026 06:36 pm IST - CHENNAI/COIMBATORE A view of Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore | Photo Credit: M.

Periasamy The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has launched a detailed inquiry into allegations of serious financial irregularities at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai and Periyar Arivulagam library at Coimbatore.

Amidst allegations that books with AI-generated content and factual mistakes were purchased at inflated rates, DVAC officers made enquiries with the library staff and took copies of certain records in both the libraries for investigation, sources in the…
The agency is looking into allegations of names of fictitious authors, fabrication of International Standard Book Number (ISBNs), depiction of factual errors and higher book prices.
During the search at Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore on Tuesday, DVAC sleuths scrutinised documents pertaining to book purchase in the administrative section of the library, on the third floor.
The DVAC would register a case if prima facie evidence is established in the detailed inquiry.

Mr. Dhinakaran wanted an elaborate investigation to be conducted into the matter and said that if the legislator was found guilty, he should be given the maximum punishment.

items.title: Minister To Parents: Sell Your Vehicle If You Can't Stop Minor Children From Driving
points: Kerala Transport Minister C P John has a blunt message for parents who allow their underage children to drive: if you cannot stop them from taking the family car or two-wheeler, sell the vehicle.
Speaking to reporters on November 10, John said parents should not hand over vehicle keys to minors.
He argued that simply advising 16- and 17-year-olds against driving was unlikely to be enough.
The warning follows a high-profile crash on October 25 in Cheranalloor, Kochi.
A Mercedes-Benz allegedly driven by a 17-year-old struck a two-wheeler, killing its rider, Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery.
The Motor Vehicles Act has a limited exception allowing eligible 16-year-olds to ride motorcycles with engines not exceeding 50cc, subject to licensing requirements.
Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act deals specifically with offences committed by juveniles.
The provision specifies a ₹25,000 fine and imprisonment of up to three years for the responsible guardian or owner.

items.title: Next-Generation Hyundai Creta Interior Spied! [Video]
points: Hyundai is set to launch the next-generation Creta in India in the first half of 2027.
The mid-size SUV is currently being actively tested in different parts of the country.
Now, a video shared on YouTube shows some interior details and features of the next-generation Creta.
This short-form video has been shared on the channel MRD Cars.
It seems to be as large as the second-generation Kia Seltos.
Previous spy shots had indicated that the new Creta could come with Hyundai’s new-age Pleos Connect infotainment system.
The outgoing Creta has 8-way power adjustments just for the driver’s seat.
The video has also confirmed that the vehicle will come with ‘Boss Mode’ adjustments that let the rear seat occupants adjust the front passenger seat using a pair of buttons.

items.title: Centre condemns coordinated anti-India campaign allegedly by Chinese vloggers presenting Dhaka locations as Delhi
points: Around 150 Chinese nationals have been reported to be documenting impoverished neighbourhoods in the Bangladeshi capital and broadcasting the footage as scenes from India, according to an investigative report published by Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo.

The ongoing operation involves Chinese vloggers filming within the narrow lanes of Tekpara and Uttara districts in Dhaka, subsequently transmitting live content across digital networks while falsely claiming that the broadcasts originate from New Delhi.

In so far as efforts by foreign elements to portray parts of Dhaka as Delhi are concerned, the peddling of false narratives only undermines the credibility of the actors involved and those behind them in such an exercise,” Mr. Jaiswal added.

The investigation highlights specific instances, including a Chinese national identified as ‘Mianmian’, who stated that she originated from China’s Sichuan province, conducting a livestream near a canal in Uttara’s Sector 12 on November 1.

The Chinese nationals are reportedly broadcasting through Chinese social media platforms, particularly Douyin, China’s domestic short-video platform, and WeChat, China’s messaging and social networking platform.

items.title: Naga ancestral remains returning home from England museum
points: Members of the Naga team that received 39 Naga artefacts, including human remains, from the Pitt Rivers Museum, University of Oxford, on November 9. | Photo Credit: AFP After more than a century in England, 39 Naga ancestral remains are returning home to…

On Monday (November 9, 2026), the University of Oxford transferred the custodianship of 39 Naga artefacts, including human remains, to a team comprising members of the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) and the Naga Tribe Hoho, the apex body of all Naga…
The formality marked a significant milestone in the Naga community’s efforts to reclaim ancestral remains held in museums abroad.
In a joint statement, the FNR and NTH said the university’s Pitt Rivers Museum hosted the handover ceremony.
This concluded an NFR-facilitated repatriation process that began in 2020.
Established in 1884, the museum received the Naga artefacts from various collectors.
The statement said Laura Van Broekhoven and Wati Aier signed the transfer document for the museum and FNR, respectively.

items.title: Akhilesh vows to make Ayodhya ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’
points: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. | Photo Credit: Shahshi Shekhar Kashyap Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav has promised to develop Ayodhya with world-class infrastructure and transform it into the "global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage" if his party comes to…

Alleging that devotees had been hurt by the "theft from the Ram temple", the former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister said his party would also introduce a transparent system for the temple to restore public confidence.
"We will provide world-class infrastructure and make Ayodhya the 'global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage'," Mr. Yadav said.

He also promised to promote traditional boating in Ayodhya to benefit local boatmen and revive the association between Lord Ram and Nishadraj, the king of Shringverpur and the leader of the Nishada, a tribal community, in the Ramayana.

Mr. Yadav alleged that the BJP was attempting to undermine this relationship because it did not want people to remember the bond between Lord Ram and the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) communities.

items.title: Karnataka Industries Minister blames Gadkari for ‘ethanol blending crisis’
points: Patil, Minister for Large and Medium Industries.

Patil on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) accused Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari of being primarily responsible for the crisis that has arisen due to allowing of ethanol to be blended with petrol allegedly beyond the prescribed limits.
Speaking to media persons here, Mr. Patil demanded a comprehensive investigation into the matter.
“They [the Centre] refuses to believe me when I speak the truth about ethanol blending.
Let them ask sugar industry leaders such as Murugesh Nirani and Prabhakar Kore.
The Minister also said ethanol stocks at sugar factories have exceeded their storage capacity.
“The problem is not confined to Karnataka; Maharashtra is facing the same situation.
Instead, Mr. Gadkari introduced the ethanol-blending system abruptly, resulting in the present crisis,” Mr. Patil alleged.

items.title: Telangana govt seeks loan relief for farmers hit by El Niño-induced drought
points: Telangana government on Tuesday requested bankers to ease the financial burden on farmers by restructuring and rescheduling their existing crop loans due to the distress in agriculture across the state caused by an El Niño-induced rainfall deficit.

Addressing a meeting of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) on Drought Relief Measures for Kharif 2026, state deputy chief minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, in-charge of finance portfolio, urged banks to extend fresh credit to farmers, enabling them…
The deputy chief minister pointed out that the government declared 365 mandals across 31 districts drought-affected, with 111 being severely affected.
He cited the all-time peak power demand of 20,018 MW recorded on October 16 as evidence of the efforts farmers made to save their standing crops despite the adverse conditions.
Tummala urged banks to achieve the Rabi season crop loan target of ₹38,268 crore to ensure farmers had access to adequate financial resources for the next cultivation cycle.

items.title: Does GTA 6 Have Fast Travel? Explained
points: Rockstar is building its biggest map yet with GTA 6’s State of Leonida, which is reportedly 2x as big as GTA 5 and 3x larger than Red Dead Redemption 2’s map.
Thankfully, players can fast travel in GTA 6, and here’s how.
GTA 6 features an in-game taxi app called Ryde Me, which players can use to fast-travel between various locations in GTA 6‘s State of Leonida.
Red Dead Redemption 2 had a slower, limited fast-travel system from your camp to a major town with a loading screen.
Thanks to the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, fast travel in GTA 6 should come with minimal downtime and no loading screens.
However, the new fast travel system seems much more streamlined, and both Jason and Lucia in GTA 6 can use the Ryde Me taxi app to book a ride whenever and wherever they want.
Sagnik Adhikary is a Gaming News Writer at Beebom with over 4 years of experience covering all sorts of news, guides, listicles, and more.

items.title: OMC stocks: Brent slips below $90 to hit over 2-month low amid Iran peace hopes; Will HPCL, BPCL and IOC benefit?
points: Shares of oil marketing companies (OMCs) are likely to be on investors' radar when the Indian stock market resumes regular trading on Wednesday, November 11, as international crude oil prices have fallen to a three-month low amid diplomatic efforts to end…
Brent crude fell towards $90 per barrel on Tuesday, extending losses from the previous session and touching its lowest level since late August.
The decline came after US President Donald Trump played down the prospect of additional military action against Iran, easing fears of prolonged supply disruptions in the Middle East.

items.title: 'Crime To Be Ambitious?' Pranab Mukherjee's Daughter Hits Back At Sonia Gandhi
points: What's wrong with it, asks Sharmistha Mukherjee, Pranab Mukherjee's daughter, about her father's prime ministerial ambition, and how it "shocked" Sonia Gandhi when the veteran leader suggested it was time for a "change at the top".

Sonia Gandhi, in her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love', which released worldwide today, references a 2010 conversation with Pranab Mukherjee and writes "he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top which I…
Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that 'ambition' was supported by decades of experience in politics & governance, hard work & a brilliant mind?" Sharmistha Mukherjee asked.

items.title: Anthropic sets IPO price band at $70-$78, targets valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
points: Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its proposed initial public offering (IPO), potentially valuing the five-year-old company at up to $1.405 trillion and positioning it for one of the largest…
According to an updated filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Tuesday, Anthropic plans to offer 825 million shares in the IPO.
At the upper end of the price band, the company could raise approximately $64.35 billion.
The proposed valuation represents a significant increase from the $965 billion valuation announced by Anthropic during its May funding round.

The AI developer had reportedly considered a $2 trillion valuation, but shareholders recently expressed doubts about achieving even $1.5 trillion, with one investor describing that figure as a 'stretch'.
If completed as scheduled, Anthropic's Nasdaq debut would come approximately five months after SpaceX completed a record-breaking IPO that raised $85.7 billion.

items.title: Russian Paraglider Gets Stuck In High-Tension Wires In Himachal, Rescued After 3-Hour Operation
points: A major tragedy was averted in Himachal Pradesh's Mandi district after a Russian paraglider got trapped in high-tension wires nearly 100 metres above the ground.
After an intense three-hour crane-assisted operation by SDRF, NDRF and NHAI, the pilot, identified as Alexey, was rescued safely.
The incident took place near Tandu in Mandi on Monday afternoon, when the paraglider got entangled in overhead power lines during a flight.
Alexey had taken off from Bir Billing, the world-famous paragliding site in Kangra district, earlier in the day.
During the flight, he somehow got caught in the high-voltage wires, leaving him suspended several metres above the ground.
Following the incident, the pilot reportedly used his mobile phone to share photographs and his location with the Bir Billing Paragliding Association.
Speaking to NDTV, Mandi Deputy Commissioner Apoorv Devgan said the administration received information in the afternoon that a paraglider was stranded on high-tension wires near Tandu.

items.title: Award-winning Keralam farmer who used his banana farming as cover for smuggling drugs arrested
points: The Ernakulam Rural police have arrested an award-winning 31-year-old farmer suspected to be running a drug network under the cover of his agriculture ventures.
Nair, aka Dani, of Haripad, Alappuzha district was arrested with 803 grams of suspected hashish oil and 8 grams of suspected MDMA, the police said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
The investigating team zeroed in on the accused as part of the probe into the recent arrest of Harikrishnan K.S., 32, of Palluruthy, Kochi with 185 gram of suspected MDMA from a lodge in Aluva.
The accused, who lives near Nanjanagudu, Mysuru, was nabbed by a special investigation team, led by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S.
He had reportedly pursued a higher education programme in Agribusiness in Germany between 2015 and 2018.
He later returned to Keralam during the floods in 2018 and ventured into farming.
The police said he had won a government award for the best young farmer in Haripad in 2022.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 9, Watch Ultra 2 Could Get HMG Edition Watch Faces, Suggests APK Teardown
points: Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 with the Qualcomm Snapdragon Wear Elite chipset and an AMOLED display arrived earlier this year alongside the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2.
Now, the company seems to be preparing exclusive versions of its Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2.
References to the customised HMG Edition watch faces for the wearables have reportedly been discovered in the Galaxy Wearable app.

As per a report by Android Authority, the APK teardown of the Galaxy Wearable companion app includes references to two customised watch faces named Ultra Performance HMG Edition and Analogue Balance HMG Edition.
The report states that the customised designs were developed for the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2.
The gifts are said to have included customised Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Buds 4 and Galaxy Watch models.
The Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 is available in 40mm and 44mm sizes in India with a starting price of Rs 37,999.

items.title: GTA 6 vs GTA 5: The Biggest Differences You Should Know
points: GTA 6 is launching more than 13 years after GTA 5 took the world by storm, and Rockstar is pushing the boundaries of what an open-world experience can be.
That said, here are the biggest differences between GTA 6 and GTA 5, showcasing how far Rockstar has come in creating the ultimate open-world experience.
The studio gives all GTA 6 characters like Jason, Lucia, and Raul an unmatched level of detail compared to GTA 5’s Michael, Trevor, and Franklin.
But all this visual fidelity comes at a cost: Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will be locked at 30 fps on all consoles, including the PS5 Pro.
So players hoping for a higher frame rate or even 60 FPS in GTA 6 might be disappointed.
Meanwhile, GTA 5 threw Michael, Trevor, and Franklin into a chaotic mix: three ex-criminals pulled back into the life of crime by corruption, debt, and a whole lot of bad decisions.

items.title: New Hyundai Creta Interiors Spied – More Space, Features
points: Now that Hyundai Bayon has been launched for an introductory price of Rs 10 lakh (Ex-sh), it is a ticket for the company to make Creta larger, more feature-rich and with higher equipment list for a more premium price tag.
Creta has grown in dimensions and has more equipment, as seen in the spy shots.
The latest spy shots show Hyundai Creta with full camouflage.
However, the video also shows some of the interior and expected features and creature comforts, showing Hyundai’s commitment of offering the fattest brochure of its segment.
In India’s Mid Size C Segment SUV space, only the Tata Sierra has Boss Mode, but it is manually operated.
Powering the new-gen Creta will be the same trio of 1.5L engines (1.5L NA Petrol, 1.5L Turbo Petrol, 1.5L Turbo Diesel).
Gearbox options will include 6-speed manual, iVT and 7-speed DCT options.
Launch could happen in 2027 and more details will follow in the future.

items.title: Sonia Gandhi Gets Her Adviser Ahmed Patel's Death Year Wrong In Memoir
points: Sonia Gandhi, writing in her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love', got the death year of her closest political advisers, Ahmed Patel, wrong.
In 2020, mourning the death of Ahmed Patel, who was believed to be part of every key decision she made, Gandhi wrote she lost an "irreplaceable comrade, faithful colleague and friend".
However, the book wrongly mentions the death year as 2022.

READ | "Irreplaceable Comrade": Sonia Gandhi Mourns "Friend" Ahmed Patel Ambika Soni, Madhavrao Scindia, joined by Ahmed Patel were part of a group Sonia Gandhi consulted on political matters during the early years of her political life.
Ahmed Patel, "AP" as he was called in the party, was the Rajya Sabha member from Gujarat and had also advised former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.
As a Youth Congress leader, he was chosen at 28 by Indira Gandhi to contest the Lok Sabha elections in 1977 from Bharuch in Gujarat.

items.title: Nvidia in Crisis! China Spy Allegations, FBI Probe, shares crash, more: Key things investors should know - Still a buy?
points: Nvidia scandal: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing intense scrutiny following reports of an alleged relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of being linked to an espionage operation.
Alice Huang served as a senior executive at Megaspeed between March and November 2023.

US and Singaporean authorities are investigating suspicions that Megaspeed helped circumvent US export restrictions by smuggling more than $2 billion worth of Nvidia AI processors, including H100 and H800 GPUs, into China.
On November 10, 2026, Nvidia shareholders filed a federal fraud lawsuit in California against the company and Huang.
Nvidia shares fell more than 4% in pre-market trading on Monday, slipping to around $178 apiece.
On November 9, the first trading day after the board's announcement, the stock declined approximately 4.2% to 6%.
The fall reportedly wiped around $7.4 billion off Huang's personal net worth in a single day, pushing him out of the world's 10 richest individuals.

items.title: "Not 2029 Elections": N Ram On The Timing Of Sonia Gandhi's Book, Its Politics
points: Sonia Gandhi's "Belonging: A Journey of Love", which was released today, will have elements that fuel the 2029 elections, but it was not written with politics mind, N Ram, the former Editor-in-Chief of the daily The Hindu said today.

In an exclusive interview with NDTV, N Ram said political issues came in course of narration in the book, which Sonia Gandhi has described as an effort to portray her family "honestly, as people (she) knew and loved".

"It happened suddenly... there are inputs for the elections in this, particularly what she says about the BJP and the RSS and how people are restless, how, you know, there's been vote stealing, how institutions have been damaged or destroyed," he told NDTV.
"She particularly mentions the Election Commission of India...
The 2029 elections are a little further away... had it been for the election, she could have had it two years down the road.
The timing of the book, he said, has been determined by feeling.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi likely to address gig workers at Congress' Bharat summit in Hyderabad
points: Telangana Congress president B Mahesh Kumar Goud on Tuesday said party leader Rahul Gandhi is likely to address a meeting of gig workers when he attends the bharat summit here on November 13 and 14.

Speaking to reporters in Delhi after meeting Gandhi, he said the Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha suggested convening a meeting of gig workers because the state government passed a welfare legislation for them.
Goud said he briefed Gandhi about the programmes taken up by the Congress in Telangana and also invited him to attend a proposed 'mega BC rally'.
"... he (Rahul Gandhi) will come to Hyderabad either on November 13 or 14 to participate in the Bharat Summit.
Along with the Bharat Summit, he may address gig workers since Telangana passed an act," he said.
The Telangana legislative assembly passed the telangana platform based gig workers (registration, social security and welfare) bill, 2026, in March this year.

Haider recalled sharing how her mother and other family members had been anxiously following the results through WhatsApp messages and phone calls.
Haider made history in the US after winning a seat in the Illinois house of representatives, becoming the first South Asian woman to be elected to the state's general assembly.

items.title: Andhra govt extends suspension of IPS officer N Sanjay till retirement or end of criminal trial
points: Amaravati, The Andhra Pradesh government on Tuesday extended the suspension of IPS officer N Sanjay until the conclusion of criminal proceedings against him or his retirement next year, whichever comes first.

Sanjay, a 1996-batch IPS officer, was placed under suspension in December 2024 over charges of misappropriation and misuse of public funds in the development, maintenance and work of the AGNI NoC web portal while working as the Director General of Andhra…

Likewise, he is also accused of "misappropriation of funds" allotted for training police personnel to create awareness among SCs and STs about the rights of victims and provisions of the Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989, while working as Additional…

items.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
points: Instead, the court went beyond Deepavali to highlight a consistent danger that sustains and would worsen the toxic air: vehicular emissions.
On November 6, the court detected a sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, for CAQM, had, at the time, submitted that a meta-analysis of studies from 2015 to 2025 attributed PM2.5 in Delhi to a mix of primary emissions and secondary particulate formation from sources within the…

Subsequently, on February 23, the court directed the Delhi government and three Ministries – Environment, Petroleum and Natural Gas, and Commerce and Industry – to submit a joint proposal for shifting coal-based industries out of Delhi NCR.
This direction was based on a CAQM recommendation to ban the establishment of new coal-based thermal power plants within a 300 km radius from Delhi.

items.title: Keralam CPI(M) awaits ICC report on complaint against former Palakkad secretary
points: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has stepped up its internal inquiry into a sexual misconduct complaint against former Palakkad district secretary E.N.
The party’s internal complaints committee (ICC) is investigating the complaint.
It has reportedly completed key procedures, including recording the statement of the woman who filed the complaint.

items.title: Gangotri Dham portals close; devotees can offer prayers at winter abode in Mukhba temple
points: The portals of Gangotri Dham officially closed for the winter season on Tuesday at 12.05pm amid chants of Vedic hymns and tunes from the Army band and traditional drums.
This year, the shrine witnessed an unprecedented footfall, with over one million devotees arriving for darshan since the portals opened on April 19, breaking all records from the past four years.
The temple was adorned with five quintals of flowers, and an Indian Army band played traditional tunes as the Utsav Doli (festive palanquin) of Goddess Ganga departed for its winter abode.
After the closure, Goddess Ganga’s palanquin began an approximately 25-kilometre journey to Mukhba village, revered as her maternal home.
The procession made its first major stop at the Bhairav temple after an 8-kilometre trek, then reached the Markandeya temple (Chandeshwari Devi temple) for an overnight halt.
“It was a divine feeling as my family was fortunate to witness the closure of the portal of the Gangotri Dham on Tuesday,” said Amrita Singh, a devotee from Nagpur, Maharashtra.

items.title: UK offshore supply chain looks overseas for growth
points: The UK’s offshore energy supply chain is increasingly looking overseas for new business as uncertainty surrounding domestic projects threatens investment, jobs and specialist engineering capacity, according to a new industry report.
Offshore Energies UK (OEUK) found that just 35% of 60 companies surveyed were confident about their UK business prospects over the next 12 months.
Meanwhile, 80% expect more future investment and growth to come from international markets.

The findings form part of OEUK’s Supply Chain Report 2026, which examines the pressures facing engineering companies, manufacturers, vessel operators, logistics providers, and other businesses supporting offshore energy developments.
The trade body identified approximately £123bn ($165.5bn) of potential UK offshore energy capital investment between 2026 and 2035 but warned that many projects remain uncertain.
According to the report, 95% of companies surveyed believe they could expand capacity if domestic offshore activity increased.
Oil and gas remains particularly important, with nine in ten surveyed companies deriving more than 20% of their revenue from the sector.

items.title: Telangana directs Gram Panchayats to open separate bank accounts for own revenue
points: Telangana Panchayat Raj and Rural Development department announced banks designated for Gram Panchayats across the State.
The move follows an amendment to Section 70(3) of the Telangana Panchayat Raj Act, 2018, through the Telangana Panchayat Raj (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2026.
The government issued orders recently notifying October 9, 2026, as the date of commencement of the amendment.

Commissioner of Panchayat Raj and Rural Employment Divya Devarajan instructed DPOs to facilitate the opening of dedicated accounts for all receipts and expenditure relating to the Own Source Revenue (OSR) of gram panchayats.
The accounts will be opened in the name of ‘OSR Account – [Gram Panchayat Name]’ at designated branches of the State Bank of India (SBI) and Union Bank of India (UBI).

The department has announced designated SBI branches for gram panchayats in 15 districts, including Mahbubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Narayanpet, Sangareddy, Siddipet, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Khammam, Rangareddy and Vikarabad.

items.title: Asyad and MOL sell ageing LR2 for $63m

The Muscat-listed company disclosed that the 2009-built Haima, held through a 50:50 joint venture with MOL, has been sold for OMR24.3m ($63.2m).

The transaction is expected to generate a gain of approximately OMR19m ($49.4m) at joint venture level, with Asyad’s share amounting to OMR9.5m ($24.7m), subject to final closing adjustments and accounting treatment.
The 110,077 dwt tanker has been part of the company’s fleet since construction.
The latest disposal follows Asyad’s September agreement to sell three older tankers for a combined OMR68.44m ($178m).
That package involved the 2011-built VLCCs Seeb and Samail, alongside the 2008-built MR tanker Al Amerat.
The company has been recycling capital from older ships into a substantial fleet expansion programme.

items.title: Chennai police arrest 36 persons in citywide crackdown on ‘rowdies’
points: MUTHUGANESAPANDY The Greater Chennai Police arrested 36 persons, including 16 history-sheeters, during a citywide crackdown on “rowdies” conducted on Monday (November 9, 2026).
On the instructions of Greater Chennai Police Commissioner A.
Amalraj, police teams led by inspectors conducted intensive checks, interrogations, and search operations across all police districts under the supervision of Deputy Commissioners of Police.

During the operation, the police apprehended and questioned 222 persons, including 185 persons classified as “rowdies” with criminal backgrounds and history sheets maintained at various police stations in Chennai.
Of them, 36 persons, including 16 history-sheeters, were arrested and remanded in judicial custody.
The police are continuing their investigation into the current criminal activities of the remaining 186 persons, including 169 history-sheeters.
A special drive to verify the antecedents and activities of “rowdies” was conducted on Tuesday in Avadi and Red Hills police districts under the Avadi Police Commissionerate.
The special drive was conducted to prevent criminal activities and maintain law and order in the commissionerate, said Avadi City Police Commissioner T.Senthil Kumar.

On November 7, during patrolling in the Kharar area, police received information about the four Ferozepur-based men allegedly involved in drug and illegal weapons trafficking.

items.title: Three bodies found across Lucknow in one day; police probe suspected murder, two other deaths

Police received information about a suspicious sack lying beneath the culvert through Dial-112 at around 9.15 am.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Md Mustaque inspected the spot, according to officials.

items.title: SoftBank shares climb 14% despite investment giant posting $7 billion quarterly loss on data-centre costs
points: SoftBank shares jumped 14% to close at JPY 3,872 on Tuesday, even as the Japanese investment giant subsequently reported a second-quarter net loss of around $7 billion.

Investors will get their first opportunity to react to SoftBank's earnings disappointment on Wednesday, after the company swung to a second-quarter net loss of $7 billion, hit by hefty investments in US data-centre projects and rising financing costs.

points: APTF State president Chennupati Manjula and general secretary K.

items.title: Norway’s IMO proposal: will more flexibility create a functioning surplus market?
points: Norway has proposed a substantial redesign of the IMO Net-Zero Framework, combining additional Surplus Units for zero- and near-zero fuels, five-year banking and broader use of surplus across both compliance tiers.
Ahead of ISWG-GHG 23 and MEPC 85, Norway has submitted two closely related proposals, ISWG-GHG 23/2/5 and ISWG-GHG 23/2/6, seeking to address concerns with the IMO Net-Zero Framework (NZF).

It would extend SU validity from two to five years, allow SUs to balance both Tier 1 and Tier 2 deficits, and with that also replace Remedial Units with Voluntary Contribution Units (VCUs) as an alternative compliance route.

What Norway’s IMO proposal is about Under Norway’s suggested 2030 trajectory, the Base Target would require a 4.8% GFI reduction against the IMO reference value of 93.3 gCO₂e/MJ, while the Direct Compliance Target would require a 17.8% reduction.
Similar to previous proposals, ships above the Base Target would face both Tier 1 and Tier 2 deficits.

items.title: Iron Ore Steadies Amid Declining Global Shipments
points: Iron ore futures steadied above CNY 680 per ton on Tuesday, remaining near four-week highs as global shipments and arrivals at Chinese ports recorded significant declines.
Industry data showed that global iron ore shipments dropped by 5.57 million tons to 29.91 million tons in the week ending November 8.
Shipments from Australia and Brazil also fell by 3.84 million tons to 24.06 million tons.
Meanwhile, arrivals at major Chinese ports declined by 2.5 million tons over the same period to 27.64 million tons.
Official figures also revealed that China’s iron ore imports fell 3.8% month-on-month in October, reaching their lowest level in five months.
Additionally, demand expectations for the key steelmaking raw material remained subdued due to production curbs in northern China driven by environmental concerns.
Industry data further indicated that average hot metal output among Chinese steelmakers, a key gauge of iron ore demand, continued to trend lower.

items.title: Refineries have shifted production away from gasoline to middle distillates
points: Particularly high refinery margins for distillate fuel oil and jet fuel have contributed to shifts in the refinery yields of major products in 2026.
The U.S. refining fleet tends to have a strong refinery yield of gasoline—typically between 45%–50%.
In general terms, for every 100 barrels of crude oil U.S. refiners process, they produce about 45–50 barrels of gasoline.
The combined yield of motor gasoline, distillate fuel oil, and jet fuel typically accounts for between 85%–90% of the petroleum products produced by the U.S. refining fleet.
Despite high gasoline prices, refinery yields of motor gasoline have trended below the five-year (2021–2025) low throughout 2026.
From January through August 2026, refinery yields of gasoline have averaged less than 45% and have been well below the five-year low in every month.
The U.S. refinery fleet exceeded an average jet fuel yield of 12% for the first time in March 2026, according to EIA data.

items.title: Norway faces 1.9 million boepd production shortfall by 2040 without major discoveries
points: For more than half a century, Norway’s oil and gas production has been underpinned by a handful of very large discoveries, the last of which, Wisting in the Barents Sea, was made more than a decade ago.
While this approach has helped sustain production in the near term, it will not be enough to arrest the NCS’s projected decline through to 2040.

items.title: Energean taps Njord Survey for North Sea decom work

The contract covers Wenlock, Garrow, and Kilmar, where survey work will assess the seabed following the removal of platforms and associated subsea infrastructure.

Njord will carry out geophysical and environmental surveys across the former platform locations and pipeline routes, using multibeam echosounders, side-scan sonar, underwater cameras and environmental sampling equipment.
The findings will be compared with earlier surveys to assess the impact of decommissioning activities and support Energean’s final reporting to UK regulators.
Njord plans to deploy its own survey vessels, equipment and personnel for the work.

items.title: US Coast Guard Airlifts 4 Oil Tanker Crew With Suspected Food Poisoning Off Puerto Rico
points: Four mariners suffering from suspected food poisoning were airlifted by a U.S. Coast Guard helicopter crew from the Cyprus-flagged oil tanker M/V Daibelli on Sunday, November 8, near Vieques, Puerto Rico.
The master of the 328-foot tanker on Saturday night informed Rescue Sub-Center San Juan about the symptoms among four of his crew.

items.title: Kongsberg Unveils Arctic Hunter Uncrewed Submarine Hunter For Royal Navy’s Hybrid Fleet
points: Kongsberg Maritime has unveiled a new uncrewed surface vessel (USV) called Arctic Hunter for the Royal Navy’s Type 92 anti-submarine warfare (ASW) requirement.

items.title: Royal Navy Launches Its First Ever Autonomous Squadron To Run Uncrewed Boats
points: Portsmouth is now home to the Royal Navy’s first autonomous squadron, a new unit set up to put uncrewed boats on the front line.

The 1st Autonomous Squadron was commissioned on November 5 at His Majesty’s Naval Base Portsmouth in the presence of over 200 guests that included navy personnel, dignitaries, media and families, according to the Royal Navy.
During the ceremony, the Kraken and Rattler uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) that the unit will run were steered around Portsmouth Harbour from a control hub.
The squadron has about 180 personnel, which is the strength of a Type 23 frigate, and they work in two watches so that operations can go on through day and night.

items.title: Black Sea Shipping Activity Falls 37% As Attacks On Merchant Ships Increase
points: Shipping activity in the Black Sea has fallen by 37% compared with last year as attacks on merchant ships and port infrastructure have increased, Ukrainian outlet Intent reported.
According to the report, 1,370 cargo ships with a deadweight of over 1,000 metric tons operated in the region’s waters in October 2026, while 2,091 vessels operated as recently as March.
Activity declined steadily every month after March, with the sharpest drop recorded in August, when the monthly number of vessels fell by more than 10%.
Container ships and bulk carriers were hit particularly hard, as their presence in the Black Sea has nearly halved since June.
They also said that the threat to commercial shipping is gradually spreading to waters near the borders of NATO countries.

items.title: New UCL tool flags food security risks from shipping emissions rules
points: The International Maritime Organization’s proposed shipping decarbonisation measures could disproportionately increase the transport costs of essential food imports, particularly for countries dependent on shipments of bulk cereals, according to new…

Researchers at UCL’s Shipping and Oceans Research Group have launched an online tool examining how different versions of the IMO’s Net-Zero Framework (NZF) could affect maritime transport costs and traded goods prices through 2050.
The NZF Impact Tracker includes a dedicated food security section covering eight essential food groups, allowing countries to identify commodities most exposed to higher shipping costs.
The analysis indicates that unprocessed cereals are particularly vulnerable because their relatively low value and high volume make freight a larger component of their delivered cost.
Countries heavily dependent on imported cereals could consequently face greater increases in food transport costs than those importing higher-value products.

Earlier research involving UCL identified Papua New Guinea, Haiti, Yemen, Solomon Islands and Liberia among countries particularly vulnerable to food security pressures associated with higher import costs.

The study says the country’s traditional advantage of offering significantly higher returns than developed markets is shrinking, which could make it harder to attract the same scale of foreign capital used to finance current account deficits in the past.
The research notes that India’s economic fundamentals remain relatively stable, supported by anchored inflation, gradual fiscal consolidation and an improving sovereign credit profile.

points: Google Gemini Memory Summary feature requires Keep Activity and Memory to be enabled.
Google's official support page currently lists US as the supported region for the feature Google has started rolling out a new Memory summary feature for its Gemini AI assistant.
The new tool is designed to provide users more control over the personal information Gemini keeps about users based on previous conversations.
Google's Memory summary feature is rolling out to Gemini users with additional controls for managing saved information.
To access the feature, users can open Gemini and navigate to Settings > Personal Intelligence > Memory summary.
According to Google's support documentation, Memory summary is available to users in the US with an active Google AI plan.
The Google Support page says users must be signed in to Gemini with a personal Google account and should be at least 18 years old.

items.title: Tata Aeris Beats Honda Amaze In October 2026 Compact Sedan Sales
points: Tata's new Aeris has overtaken the Honda Amaze in the October 2026 sedan sales ranking.
Tata dispatched 4,005 Aeris sedans to dealerships, compared with 3,337 units of the Amaze.
That gave the Aeris a lead of 668 cars, or roughly 20% more volume than its Honda rival, and placed it third among the ten sedans tracked by AutoPunditz.
The result is encouraging for Tata because the Aeris was launched only on September 25, with customer deliveries scheduled to begin from October 11.
The Tata Aeris was launched at an introductory ex-showroom price of Rs 5.29 lakh for the entry petrol manual.
Its five trim levels are Smart, Pure, Pure+, Creative and Accomplished, and the most expensive CNG AMT is listed at Rs 9.74 lakh.
The Honda Amaze currently starts at approximately Rs 7.65 lakh for the newer-generation model, while Honda also lists an older-generation Amaze at a lower price.
That makes the starting-price difference between the Aeris and the new Amaze roughly Rs 2.36 lakh.

items.title: "Respect Privacy": C Naidu To Workers On Pawan Kalyan's Separation With Wife
points: Both ruling and opposition sides came together to prevent the personal announcement from becoming another flashpoint in Andhra Pradesh's politically charged social media environment.
The TDP-affiliated iTDP social media wing issued a warning against personal attacks on political leaders and their families, covering both ruling alliance and opposition leaders.
It said inappropriate posts, discussions and comments would not be tolerated and warned of disciplinary action against accounts associated with the organisation.
The YSRCP Central Office also issued an official note addressed to party leaders, spokespersons, cadre and social media activists.
"Please respect privacy and exercise discretion in public communications," the YSRCP communication said.
Pawan Kalyan has frequently been at the centre of political exchanges between the two camps, with personal references sometimes becoming part of public political discourse.
Pawan Kalyan and Anna announced their decision to part ways after 13 years of marriage through a joint statement circulated on Monday night.
On Tuesday, Pawan Kalyan attended the cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu at the state secretariat.

items.title: "Even When There Is No Stubble Burning...": AAP Attacks BJP Over Pollution
points: Punjab's stubble-burning controversy has once again triggered a political war of words, with Cabinet Minister Barinder Kumar Goyal accusing the Delhi government of repeatedly blaming Punjab for the national capital's pollution while ignoring its own…
Reacting to the allegations linking Punjab's stubble burning to Delhi's deteriorating air quality, Goyal said that blaming Punjab had become a convenient political excuse for Delhi.
"People in Delhi have only one thing to say - Punjab is responsible for pollution.
Even when there is no stubble burning, they continue to claim that pollution is coming from Punjab," the minister said.
Questioning the logic behind attributing Delhi's pollution to farm fires in Punjab, Goyal argued that the smoke from Punjab does not simply travel directly to Delhi, bypassing Haryana.

The minister maintained that the Bhagwant Mann-led Punjab government had put comprehensive arrangements in place to tackle stubble burning and had taken several measures to encourage farmers to manage paddy residue without setting it on fire.
